name: Scoria Ravine
geological_features: Deep ravines carved by ancient lava rivers now partially cooled
Scoria fields of lightweight volcanic rock
Collapsed lava tube networks forming trench systems
description: Scoria Ravine is a mid-sized volcanic world scored with deep ravines that were carved by ancient lava rivers. The lava has largely cooled, leaving behind channels lined with obsidian and floored with rough scoria rubble. Between the ravines, the surface is covered in fields of lightweight volcanic rock that crumbles underfoot, making overland travel treacherous.

The toxic atmosphere hangs heavy and still in the ravines, concentrating volcanic gases to lethal densities. Above the ravine lips, winds scatter ash and scoria fragments in abrasive gusts. The planet's color palette is uniformly dark: black obsidian, gray scoria, rust-red oxidized iron, all under a perpetually overcast sky.

Scoria Ravine appears to be in a transitional geological phase, its volcanic activity waning as its core cools. The great lava rivers that carved the ravines have dwindled to scattered vents and fumaroles. In geological time, the planet is dying, its fires guttering out one by one.

The ravine systems offer sheltered corridors for transit across the surface, and the aluminum deposits in the scoria fields have modest commercial value. Scoria Ravine serves primarily as a waypoint and refueling stop for ships operating in the outer system. Its ravines, with their obsidian walls catching the dim light, possess a stark beauty that some travelers find worth the detour.
